invariant-rustbv-u128-chunking: RustBV::Concrete is u128-backed (max 128 bits). Any Python->Rust memory or register sync that takes 'data: &[u8]' and packs all bytes into a u128 via 'value |= (b as u128) << (i * 8)' is BUGGY for data.len() > 16. In release mode, shifts >= 128 mask to 7 bits — bytes 16..31 OR back into low bytes, then store_concrete's page-fill loop replays the same masking, painting a 16-byte-repeating pattern across the claimed width. Found via angr-5aj8 (2026-06-06): baby-re under ANGR_RUST_USE_CALLBACK_MEMORY_PROXY=1 corrupted stack with witness pattern. Safe pattern: split into 16-byte chunks per RustSimState::apply_changes in state.rs (loop 'while offset < bytes.len(): chunk_size = remaining.min(16); ...'). Fixed sites: _set_state_memory_concrete (state_api.rs), _pending_memory_store (pending_api.rs), RustSimState::memory_store (state.rs). REMAINING SITES TO AUDIT: register-write path in apply_changes (state.rs:2294-2301) does NOT chunk — would corrupt YMM (32B) / ZMM (64B) wide-register writes. claripy_bridge.rs:1865 'bytes_to_u128' has 'if i < 16' guard so it just drops high bytes (less catastrophic but still wrong).
invariant-rustbv-zero-width:
RustBV with width=0 is supported on BOTH paths. RustBV::concrete(value, 0) collapses the mask to 0 so any value normalizes to 0. Since angr-fs8kb.28 the symbolic path is safe too: RustBV::from_parts returns Concrete{value:0,width:0} for width 0 instead of calling z3::ast::BV::new_const(name, 0) — Z3 has no 0-width BV sort, so that panicked inside the sort constructor and, under panic="abort", SIGABRTed the whole process (not a catchable Python exception). The fix sits in from_parts because all three symbolic construction paths funnel through it: RustBV::symbolic, RustBV::symbolic_with_id (claripy BVS import via claripy_bridge::import), and the From<RustBVData> snapshot/deserialize arm — plus RustSolverContext::create_symbolic, which reaches it through RustSymbolTable::create_symbolic. It is placed BEFORE the #[cfg(feature="vex-engine-z3")] split so the no-z3 build agrees with the z3 one. Collapsing symbolic->concrete is correct, not merely safe: the empty bitvector has exactly one inhabitant, so no constraint can distinguish two width-0 leaves; that is why it stays infallible rather than plumbing a Result through three infallible signatures. Note check_bv_width (width_guards.rs) still DELIBERATELY permits width 0 at both trust boundaries — the guard is a max-width cap, not a zero-width reject, so do not add a width>0 check there.

OBLIGATION this places on every op: because create_concrete(0,0) is reachable from Python and every op_* in solver/handle_api.rs accepts the resulting handle, each op's CONCRETE arm in symbolic/value_ops.rs must tolerate w == 0 — no bare '% w', no 'w - 1', no '1 << w' assuming w >= 1. define_rotate_pair!'s arm computed 'amt = a % (w as u128)', an unconditional Rust panic in EVERY profile (not gated by overflow-checks, and a process abort under panic='abort'), i.e. a Python-triggerable DoS (angr-309bq). 'No VEX IROp has a 0-bit operand' is NOT a sufficient reachability argument — the handle API is a second, wider entry point into the same value ops. Prefer the mathematically correct degenerate answer (a rotate of the empty bitvector is the identity, so w==0 folds into the existing amt==0 arm) over erroring. Property-test sweeps that 'skip width 0' for an op are a marker that this hole was noticed and left open — value_ops_property_tests.rs's rotate/reverse cross-check carried exactly that skip.
invariant-rustdoc-intra-doc-links:
Rustdoc intra-doc links in native/angr/src (updated angr-z3672, 2026-08-11). THREE authoring rules:
(1) A bare [`method_name`] never resolves — rustdoc only resolves names in *module* scope, so associated items need [`m`](Self::m) or [`Type::m`].
(2) An outer `///` doc comment on a `mod x;` DECLARATION makes rustdoc resolve *every* fragment of that module's docs — including the `//!` block inside x.rs — in the scope of the DECLARING module, not x's own. So `super::` shifts up one level and bare in-module item links break, silently, in a file you never touched. This was the root cause of 46 of the 100 warnings (run_loop_{single,steady,wave,worker} + scheduler, all declared with outer docs in exploration/mod.rs). Fix used: keep the module doc in the file's `//!` header and demote the declaration-site comment to plain `//`. Never pair an outer `///` on `mod x;` with a `//!` block in x.rs.
(3) Targets that can NEVER resolve under cargo doc — `#[cfg(test)]` items, `macro_rules!` names, items private-by-module — get a plain code span; never widen visibility just to make a doc link resolve. Note the *linking* item's visibility matters too: a `pub fn` doc linking to a private sibling trips `private_intra_doc_links` even though the target exists (5 of the angr-xtjm8 9: filesystem/ops.rs alloc_fd/offset_position, state/process.rs round_alloc_size). A pub(crate) linker with a pub(crate) target is fine. The crate-root `//!` block counts as public docs, so it may not link into pub(crate) modules at all.
GATE: --document-private-items is load-bearing (angr-sqfj8.144) — nearly every item here is pub(crate)/private, so without it rustdoc visits almost none of the docs and the lane passes with 83 broken links in the tree. Do not drop it.
LOCAL GATE (angr-z3672): the lane no longer lives only in CI. .claude/hooks/cargo-check-stop.sh runs the exact ci.yml command after clippy, under the same 'only when .rs files are dirty' guard — ~4.3s warm on the dev profile, ~0.3s when unchanged. That closes the regrowth loop this class kept riding (the box has no GitHub network, so CI never fires here). Do not remove it without replacing it in tools/ralph-gate.sh.
REFINEMENT of (3) re macro_rules! (angr-5mnx3.8): a `macro_rules!` name is resolvable by intra-doc links, but only TEXTUALLY AFTER its definition — callbacks/mod.rs has had [`with_callback_fields`] links resolving fine for months at sites below the macro_rules! block. Adding the same link to the file's `//!` module header (textually FIRST, before the definition) fails with 'exists in this crate, but it is not in scope at this link's location' — AND that one failure makes rustdoc re-report every other link to the same name, so a one-line doc edit can surface N errors at lines you never touched. Do not chase those; fix the out-of-scope one (demote it to a plain `code span!` per rule 3) and the rest go quiet.
SCOPE (angr-pr0tj, 2026-08-28): the gate is `cargo doc --workspace`, not `--manifest-path native/angr/Cargo.toml`. It was pinned at the latter in BOTH ci.yml's `Rustdoc link check` step and .claude/hooks/cargo-check-stop.sh, so the workspace's other member, native/angr-macros, was never documented and the pub `MergePolicy` derive's two links to the private VALID_MERGE_POLICIES / MECHANICAL_MERGE_POLICIES consts (a textbook rule-3 violation) sat red from the day it was written. Rules (1)-(3) apply to every member crate, not just native/angr/src. CI's clippy lane never had this hole — it runs from the repo root with no --manifest-path — and since angr-h3tx0 the Stop hook's clippy matches it. Keep any new gate command workspace-scoped so a member crate is covered on arrival. CARGO SUBTLETY the angr-h3tx0 measurement turned up: a --manifest-path-pinned clippy is NOT wholly blind to the other member — a workspace path dependency is not --cap-lints'ed, so angr-macros' *lib* was linted all along. What --manifest-path loses is --all-targets reach: only the pinned package's test/bench/example targets are selected, so a warning inside angr-macros' #[cfg(test)] mods, tests/compile_fail.rs or the trybuild ui harness scored 0 errors pinned and 2 workspace-wide. The same asymmetry does NOT hold for cargo doc, which never visits a dependency's docs at all — which is why the rustdoc half of this hole was total and the clippy half was partial.

invariant-scan-cap-defer-not-truncate:
Scan-cap policy for native SimProcedures (procedures/): a caller-supplied length n that exceeds the module scan cap (MAX_STRING_SCAN / MAX_SCAN = 4096) must NOT be silently clamped -- clamping yields a truncated answer that diverges from libc and the Python engine. Bail with Err(ProcedureError::MaxIterations(n)) so the call defers to Python. Three shapes, pick by whether the capped prefix can pin the true answer:
(1) UNCONDITIONAL bail (NativeStrncpy in strcpy.rs; NativeMemrchr in strchr.rs) -- use when no prefix result survives truncation. memrchr wants the LAST match in n bytes, so a match past the cap would override whatever the prefix found.
(2) CONDITIONAL on the cap outcome being unobservable (NativeStrncat in strcat.rs) -- scan_concrete_bounded returns (buf, null_found), so it bails only when !null_found; an oversized n whose src terminator lands inside the cap produces exactly the unbounded copy.
(3) CONDITIONAL on the prefix pinning the answer (NativeMemchr/NativeRawmemchr in strchr.rs, via helper forward_match_is_conclusive) -- a concrete non-NULL address is the true FIRST match regardless of the unscanned tail, so it stays native; a concrete NULL (absent from prefix) or a symbolic ITE chain (may still be NULL) bails. rawmemchr is always in the capped case since its bound is unbounded; its contract guarantees the byte is present, so 'absent from the first 4096' means past the cap, never NULL.
Prefer (2)/(3) when applicable -- they keep the native path for the common case. Delivered by angr-9ke6b.109 (strncat) and angr-9ke6b.108 (memchr family).
DECIDING PYTHON FACT for the no-caller-n case (an unbounded C string where the 4096 cap itself runs out): the Python engine NEVER truncates. angr/procedures/libc/strlen.py::strlen.run starts at state.libc.max_str_len (128) and, while the null-search constraints are all-false, keeps DOUBLING the window, raising SimMemoryLimitError once it passes 0x10000. So a native 4096-byte prefix is wrong twice over -- for a truly unterminated string (Python errors) and for a long-but-terminated one whose NUL sits in 4096..0x10000 (Python renders it in full). Hence sprintf_conv.rs::render_conversion's %s conversion argument bails on !null_found (angr-6fg46), shape (2) with no n. The one deliberate exception is getenv.rs::read_cstring_tolerant, which documents at its own definition why it returns the prefix.
invariant-scan-window-bounds-whole-subje: Fixed byte-scan caps in native string procs bound the ENTIRE subject sequence — whitespace + sign + base/hex prefix + digits/fraction/exponent — not just the region the cap is named after. The tempting comment 'hitting the cap is fine, parsing stops at the first non-matching byte anyway' is WRONG whenever the proc also reports a consumed-length: endptr and the accumulated value are computed relative to the truncated buffer, so a too-long input yields an endptr landing mid-run and a short value (strtol base 2: 2^53 instead of 2^60; strtod: 1e255 instead of 1e300, and a literal sitting past the cap's worth of leading whitespace reported 'no conversion' outright). Correct shape, now implemented twice — strtol.rs::read_subject_bytes and strtod.rs::read_literal_bytes: double the window while its last byte could still continue the subject sequence, stopping at a concrete null, an unconsumable byte, a symbolic byte, or a documented+tested hard ceiling (both use 4096). The continuation predicate is a deliberate over-approximation (the base/form is not known before the parser runs) and its shared half lives in procedures/ctype.rs::may_continue_numeric_subject so the two windows cannot drift; strtod adds '.'. Symbolic paths keep the small cap: an ITE accumulator costs one term per byte. Any future read_bytes_until_null / scan_concrete_bounded caller that reports a consumed length needs the same treatment. Sibling of invariant-recognizer-parser-grammar-parity.
invariant-scanf-format-error-propagation: format_common::read_format_string (procedures/) is the single home for reading a printf/scanf-family format string: it delegates to strings::scan_concrete_bounded bounded by MAX_FORMAT_LEN, so memory_load faults and symbolic bytes propagate as Err (Python fallback) rather than the old 'Err(_) => break' silent-truncation that committed symbolic stores on a corrupted format. It takes &mut RustSimState (scan_concrete_bounded needs it). extract_concrete_arg on a symbolic format byte already errored via ?; only the memory_load-failure path was swallowed. Formerly two private copies, scanf.rs::read_format_string and sprintf.rs::read_string, merged in angr-0jh0j.44 — a %s conversion argument is NOT a format string and scans against strings::MAX_STRING_SCAN instead.
invariant-scanf-length-modifier-store-wi: scanf/printf length modifiers: BOTH consumers must resolve conversion width through LengthModifier::int_conv_bits(arch_bits) in procedures/format_common.rs — parse_scanf_format (procedures/scanf_spec.rs, takes arch_bits) and the sprintf-side parse_conversion_spec/render_conversion pair (procedures/sprintf_spec.rs + sprintf_conv.rs, reads state.arch().bits() once). Widths mirror format_parser.py int_len_mod's sim_types: hh->8, h->16, none->32, ll/j->64 always (SimTypeLongLong), l/z/t->arch_bits (SimTypeLong / SimTypeLength, so 32 on ILP32 x86/arm32). Two failure modes if this is hardcoded: ScanfSpec.bits drives state.memory_store(ptr, sym_val) (writes bits/8 bytes) and record_stdin_symbol, so an over-wide bits silently clobbers adjacent guest bytes with unconstrained symbols; on the sprintf side an over-wide mask renders %ld of a bit-31-set value as the zero-extended 64-bit number where Python prints the sign-folded 32-bit one. Regression test patterns: assert_scanf_store_width_arch in scanf_tests.rs (pre-fills 8 concrete 0xAA guard bytes, asserts exactly N low bytes symbolic and the rest still 0xAA) and sprintf_one_arch in sprintf_tests.rs; both take an arch string so ILP32 is covered. Fixed in 4a1dcf6fd (angr-vfhyx, hh/h) and angr-9ke6b.111 (l/z/t arch width).
invariant-seg-selector-32bit-wrap: x86g_use_seg_selector (handle_x86_use_seg_selector in native/angr/src/vex/ccall/mod.rs, reached from handle_ccall_with_ctx's name dispatch — it was inline in handle_ccall_with_ctx before the angr-5mnx3.60 helper split) returns a 64-bit value whose LOW 32 bits are the linear address and whose BIT 32 is the error flag. The empty-descriptor-table flat-addressing fast path must compute (seg_selector<<16)+virtual_addr with a mod-2^32 wrap, matching Python's engines/vex/claripy/ccall.py x86g_use_seg_selector which does the add over 32-bit BVs then .zero_extend(32). Doing the add in u64 (the pre-d7f2db812 bug) lets a carry out of bit 31 land on bit 32 and be misread as a bad-selector error — reachable with ANY negative displacement off a segment register (mov %gs:-0x4,%eax => va=0xFFFFFFFC), not just exotic inputs. General lesson: when porting a claripy-BV computation to Rust u64, the BV width IS part of the semantics; any place the native path widens the arithmetic can leak a carry into a neighbouring ABI field. Pinned by test_use_seg_selector_gdt_empty_wraps_mod_2_32 in vex/ccall_tests.rs. Also noted: Python's own bad() builds BVV(1<<32, 32), which claripy truncates to 0 before zero_extend — the native path deliberately returns the ABI-correct 1<<32 instead of mirroring that upstream quirk.
invariant-selection-order-determinism: Selection-seam order-determinism contract (angr-op0dn.10.5, single-worker only). Two chokepoints decide dispatch order: SelectionPolicy::select (only pop site, run_loop.rs) and SelectionPolicy::on_fork (only push site). Two helpers reach on_fork, both via StashManager::push_active: helpers.rs::push_to_active_or_drop (successor/fork path, honors max_active_states) and helpers.rs::push_to_stash (angr-0jh0j.19 — stash-generic; routes a STASH_ACTIVE destination through push_active and anything else through StashManager::push_checked, the typo-warning twin of push). As of angr-1o7i0 push_to_stash is the sanctioned insertion path for EVERY state_lifecycle.rs entry point whose destination stash comes from Python (_create_state, _add_state, _fork_state_to_stash, _merge_states, _move_state, both _move_states branches) plus native_technique.rs::move_state_by_id — no Python-API raw push_back remains. A move into active counts as an insertion even though it is not a fork: it is the mirror of the on_state_removed those same paths fire when a state LEAVES active outside policy.select. A new insertion path into active MUST use one of the two helpers, never sm.ensure_stash(STASH_ACTIVE).push_back. Note push_to_stash's non-active arm must use push_checked, not push: push goes through StashManager::entry, which skips ensure_stash's unknown-stash typo warning that tests/engines/rust/test_misc.py::TestStashNameValidation pins. Invariants any new policy MUST hold: (1) terminate the ranking key with the front index i so ties break by insertion order; (2) on_fork push_back so deque order is a pure function of forks_out Vec order from core_outcome_handlers.rs; (3) NEVER iterate the per-policy HashMap/HashSet fields (CoverageGuided::seen, FindDirected::seen, LoopHeadRoundRobin::dispatched, DirectedCfgDistance::{distances,dispatched}) — only get/contains/entry. Rust HashMap seeds a fresh hasher per INSTANCE, so a single 'for (k,v) in map' in a select path makes dispatch order vary run-to-run within one process. Guarded by test_selection_trace_deterministic_across_runs in selection_policy_tests.rs (moved out-of-line from selection_policy.rs's inline test module in angr-5mnx3.21); test_selection_traces_differ_across_policies keeps it from passing vacuously. on_fork coverage is guarded behaviourally by the SpyPolicy forked-log tests in state_lifecycle_tests.rs and native_technique_tests.rs — stash contents are byte-identical with or without the chokepoint, so the policy callback log is the ONLY observable. Contract does NOT extend to the parallel scheduler — steal order is design-nondeterministic, contract there is set-equality.
invariant-shared-native-proc-dispatch:
Native SimProcedure dispatch is now ONE fn: exploration/native_proc_dispatch.rs::dispatch_native_proc (angr-ph300.73, commit e3a59dec9). Both callers consume it -- step_one's hook arm (run_loop_single.rs) and handle_simprocedure_core (core_outcome_handlers.rs). NativeProcDisposition + NativeProcCounters + segfault_message live in native_proc_dispatch.rs too; core_outcome_handlers re-exports segfault_message under #[cfg(test)] so core_outcome_tests/errors.rs' 'use super::handlers::segfault_message' still resolves.

TWO deliberate caller-parameterized divergences -- do NOT 'simplify' them away without a behavior review:
1. mirror_segfault: only the core/parallel path terminal-errors a STRICT_PAGE_ACCESS unmapped-page fault natively (NativeProcDisposition::Segfault). step_one passes false and still bounces to Python via the ordinary fallback counters. Unifying is a real behavior change.
2. The SubCall (ProcOutcome::CallAndResume) counter bump is NOT done inside dispatch_native_proc -- core bumps native_calls/call_counts the moment call_ex returns, step_one only once setup_native_subcall succeeds (and books a python_fallback + other_fallbacks_by_name on failure). Both preserved by leaving the bump caller-side.

The LANDING (return-reg write, PC/SP) stays caller-owned on purpose: step_one resolves the return address via the calling convention (get_return_addr + pops_return_addr, so ARM/ARM64/MIPS LR/X30/$ra work) while the core path is handed return_addr by the interpreter. TRAP that this caller-owned landing already produced ONCE (angr-sqfj8.37, commit a2fc5cc9b): only the RETURN-ADDRESS SOURCE legitimately differs between the two callers -- the SP ADJUSTMENT does not. Both must gate the +ptr_size bump on pops_return_addr, because on ARM/ARM64/MIPS nothing was pushed and the bump discards a live stack slot. core_outcome_handlers had NO gate for months while step_one did; it is invisible to the amd64 corpus (every bench/pytest is amd64), so only a per-arch unit test catches it. Regression: core_outcome_tests/native_return.rs::native_return_leaves_sp_untouched_on_link_register_abis (+ the amd64/x86 control native_return_advances_sp_on_stack_return_abi), driven by dispatch_hook_on_arch(arch, sp, cfg). Any future edit to either landing site: diff the two arms and check the arch-dependent halves agree.

Borrow gotcha in step_one: the registry entry must be .cloned() (cheap Arc) before calling, because the dispatcher needs &mut self.profiling.native_proc_stats alongside it.
invariant-single-string-opcode-parse: VEX opcode parsing has exactly ONE entry point: the string-based parse_opcode in vex/opcode_map.rs. There is no numeric/u32 opcode table (parse_opcode_from_u32 was deleted). The native libVEX FFI lifter (vex/libvex_lifter.rs::c_op) converts its IROp discriminant back to the pyvex name via libvex_ffi.rs::enum_names::irop_name (generated by build.rs::generate_pyvex_ffi_enum_names from the vendored cdef, never hand-edited) and then calls parse_opcode; an unknown discriminant becomes the synthetic name Iop_UNKNOWN_<n>. Consequence: adding one string arm covers BOTH lifters — there is no second table to keep in sync. Same shape as parse_type (see invariant-parse-type-width-not-none).
invariant-skip-hook-stack-lifo-pop: Zero-length-hook skip tokens are a true LIFO stack, not a set. Consumption lives in ONE place: RustExplorationManager::consume_skip_hook (exploration/pending_api.rs), called from step_one in run_loop_single.rs. It expires stale entries (expiry <= steps) then pops only the topmost match via rposition+remove. Do NOT reintroduce a retain()-based removal there: _set_skip_hook_addr pushes without dedup, so nested zero-length hooks at the same PC hold multiple tokens, and a blanket retain collapses them all at once, leaving the second occurrence unskipped and re-arming the infinite loop the skip stack prevents (angr-9ke6b.47). _clear_skip_hook_for_addr intentionally KEEPS clear-all semantics -- it is an explicit Python-side reset, not a consumption. A non-empty skip_hook_stack also forces must_run_serial (angr-04tw3.1), since no parallel path consumes it -- which is why a leaked entry is not harmless and why load_snapshot_bytes clears the stack (angr-0jh0j.12, see invariant-snapshot-load-pending-world-teardown). (The pre-bd 'GAP 6' label this mechanism used to carry was stripped in angr-6cp06.17.)
invariant-snapshot-flush-parked-bounces: PARALLEL SNAPSHOT INVARIANT (angr-op0dn.13.10): the wave path parks bounce states OUTSIDE every stash. process_parallel_bounce_queue (run_loop.rs) surfaces at most one need_callback event per run() and stores the undispatched rest in RustExplorationManager::pending_parallel_bounces — a Vec<(RustSimState, BounceKind, u64)> that is in NO stash. StashManager::dump_snapshot only serializes stashes, so any snapshot taken while bounces are parked silently loses those states AND their whole subtree; the active-PC fingerprint still looks healthy because the parked states were never counted. Symptom: an in-memory resume reaches every leaf while a snapshot resume of the same frontier reaches far fewer (pbounce synthetic, workers=4: 8/8 in-memory vs 3/8 from the snapshot). FIX: dump_snapshot_bytes calls flush_parked_bounces_to_active (run_loop.rs), which set_pc's each parked bounce to bounce_target_addr(kind) (Hook / SimProcedurePython entry — the state is parked AT the call site with the callback not yet run, so re-entry is a faithful replay) and route_successor's it back to active. SAME SHAPE for live steady parallel sessions (angr-op0dn.13.6): under RUST_PARALLEL_STEADY the frontier is resident in worker Z3 contexts and belongs to NO stash, so dumping StashManager mid-session silently truncates the search. Fix: RustExplorationManager::dump_snapshot_bytes (manager_methods_snapshot.rs) takes &mut self and calls steady_config_guard(); Python dump_snapshot calls _finalize_parallel_session() first. THE READ-ONLY CENSUS HALF (angr-03vl4.15): accessors taking &self cannot flush, so active_count and stash_counts instead ADD RustExplorationManager::parked_bounces_flushable_count (run_loop.rs), which mirrors the flush's own two filters (an id already resident in a stash is a duplicate the flush drops; a kind with no re-enterable entry address never reaches a stash) so the census is invariant across a flush; it early-returns 0 on an empty queue, so the serial path pays nothing. found_count deliberately takes NO addend — a parked bounce is a live frontier state whose callback has not run, not a collected result, and found_count gates num_find control flow in all three run loops and in push_found_capped. A stash-only view is spelled stash_count(STASH_ACTIVE). RULES for future work: (1) any NEW pymethod that reads self.sm must call the steady guard — reading self.sm without it is the silent-data-loss shape; (2) any manager-level Vec/Map that holds owned RustSimStates outside self.sm (pending_parallel_bounces, pending_callbacks) is invisible to the snapshot — a new one MUST either be serialized or flushed into a stash by the dump guard, next to steady_config_guard; (3) a new read-only census accessor must add the parked bucket the way active_count does.
invariant-snapshot-load-finalize-symmetr: Snapshot dump/load must be SYMMETRIC on the finalize contract. dump_snapshot_bytes (manager_methods_snapshot.rs, renamed from manager_methods_stats.rs in angr-03vl4.25) calls steady_config_guard() + flush_parked_bounces_to_active() before serializing self.sm; load_snapshot_bytes (angr-ph300.21), its sibling in the same module, must equally steady_config_guard() and clear pending_callbacks / pending_parallel_bounces / current_stepping_state_id BEFORE swapping self.sm. Otherwise the next run() finalizes the OLD steady session into the RESTORED stashes (two explorations merged) and a parked need_callback can resume a discarded pre-load state. Any future field added to the parked/pending set (things referencing live/worker states outside a stash) must be cleared here too. Regression: test_load_snapshot_clears_parked_pending_callback in test_manager_core.py parks a callback via symbolic SimProc arg then asserts pending_callback_ids() empty post-load.
invariant-snapshot-load-pending-world-te: RustExplorationManager::load_snapshot_bytes (exploration/manager_methods_snapshot.rs) replaces self.sm WHOLESALE, so every manager-level field that describes the PRE-restore exploration must be torn down there by hand. Current teardown inventory: steady_config_guard() (drains a live steady session first), pending_callbacks, pending_parallel_bounces, current_stepping_state_id (angr-ph300.21), skip_hook_stack (angr-0jh0j.12), plus a policy.on_state_removed() notify loop over the outgoing STASH_ACTIVE ids (angr-0jh0j.13). RULE: any NEW transient/pending manager field (mod.rs, outside self.sm) must be added to that list — 'it auto-expires' is not an excuse. skip_hook_stack was the counterexample: its (addr, expiry) tokens expire on expiry <= self.steps, but self.steps is manager-level and is NOT rewound by a restore, and must_run_serial() reads the stack with a bare is_empty(), so a leaked entry forced the restored session serial and could silently skip a same-address hook once. invariant-snapshot-quiescent-scope: SymContext snapshot quiescence: SymContextSnapshot deliberately drops all push/pop scope state (bare_z3_push_depth, scope_savepoints, scope_path), so to_snapshot/restore_from_snapshot are only valid with NO open scope. invariant-sp-bp-are-full-width: arch alias tables: 'sp'/'bp' are the ARCHITECTURE-INDEPENDENT full-width stack/base pointer on every arch, NOT the legacy 16-bit x86 sub-registers. archinfo: AMD64 sp=(48,8) bp=(56,8); X86 sp=(24,4) bp=(28,4). invariant-stash-moves-maintain-index:
StashManager::state_index is a HINT, not an authority — but code must still maintain it. Two halves, both durable:

(1) WRITE side. Any code that re-homes a state by touching `sm.stashes_mut()` / `sm.get_mut(stash)` directly MUST pair the move with `sm.index(sid, dest)`, and a move that DISCARDS the state must pair `sm.unindex(sid)` with `sm.remove_root(sid)` (module invariant I6 — index and state_roots travel together). The safe alternatives that do this for you: `push`, `push_active`, `push_or_drop_terminal`, `take_state`, `take_state_from`, `clear`. angr-c7xno.97 found NativeTechnique's Timeout arm and `evict_active_states` (shared by LengthLimiter + LoopBound) bypassing this while `park_states_at_address` / `move_state_by_id` in the SAME file did it right — so it is an oversight class, not a pattern. The I6 assert in `push_or_drop_terminal` does NOT catch it: these paths never call `push_or_drop_terminal`.

(2) READ side (angr-c7xno.97 fix). All three lookups — `find_state`, `find_state_mut`, `take_state` — now route through the private `StashManager::locate_state` helper, which accepts the indexed stash ONLY after finding the state in it and otherwise falls through to a full scan. So a future write-side bypass degrades to O(n), never to a spurious 'state N not found'. Before the fix only `find_state` self-healed; `find_state_mut`/`take_state` trusted a present-but-stale entry and returned None for a LIVE state — an observable read-vs-write divergence, since Python's `sync_state_index` only runs AFTER each run() batch returns, not mid-run.

If you add a fourth lookup, build it on `locate_state`, not on a raw `state_index.get()`.

invariant-state-id-never-reused:
INVARIANT (angr-r4r7, 2026-05-10): Rust state IDs are monotonically allocated and never reused. Once a state ID is absent from every Rust stash (active|found|avoid|deadended), it is unreachable forever. This is what makes it safe to drop Python-side shadow mappings keyed by state_id (_state_roots, _predicate_matched_ids, _py_state_options, _py_state_globals) inside _cleanup_state_cache (rust_manager.py::_cleanup_state_cache). Future shadow structures keyed by state_id should follow the same pattern: prune against any_stash in _cleanup_state_cache rather than inventing per-structure LRU caps.

EXCEPTION (angr-fs8kb.89 / .90, 2026-09-23): snapshot restore RESURRECTS ids. StashManager::from_snapshot (stash.rs) rebuilds state_index from each state's own state_id(), so RustExplorationManager::load_snapshot_bytes brings back states under their ORIGINAL ids -- ids that were, between the dump and the load, absent from every stash. The 'a stale entry can only name a dead id' argument that lets _reset_for_stage (state_lifecycle.rs) keep ConstraintTracker's skip_find_predicate_states / skip_avoid_predicate_states therefore does NOT hold across load_snapshot_bytes, which clears them (and uniqueness_set, whose content-keyed hashes would drop the whole restored frontier). Any id-keyed side table must be cleared or rebuilt at that entry point, not just pruned against the live stashes. BOTH SIDES: the Python mirror of this is rust_manager.py::_reset_python_shadow_maps_for_restore, called from load_snapshot -- it clears _predicate_matched_ids/_predicate_found/_predicate_eval_cache/_state_roots/_py_state_options/_py_state_globals. _invalidate_state_export_cache is NOT sufficient for these: it only unsets scratch.rust_fully_synced, which re-reads a mirror's CONTENTS from Rust (right for _state_cache, wrong for maps holding a verdict or a lineage). A new id-keyed dict on the Python manager must be added to that helper too.

invariant-stepping-decomposition:
The deferred-fork materialization logic exists in FOUR intentionally-distinct variants (2 sequential x 2 profiling levels), and the fork counters do NOT tally uniformly across them:
(1) fork_materialize::materialize_deferred_forks (exploration/fork_materialize.rs) — the full-profiling materializer used by resume.rs (3 callback-resume sites) and run_loop_single.rs. Per-fork solver_fork_time_ns/solver_fork_count + solver_sat_* + a batch deferred_fork_time_ns/deferred_fork_count timer. Only variant that calls reconstruct_deferred_fork_condition when the condition is absent from stored_conditions.
(2) core_outcome_handlers::materialize_deferred_forks_core — parallel-scheduler mirror of (1) via ParallelProfiling::add; stored conditions ONLY, no reconstruct fallback.
(3) SimulationLoop::process_deferred_forks_into (exploration/stepping.rs) — the simpler helper used by SimProc-native resume, SymbolicJumpTarget, and the unmodeled-call generic skip (stepping_bounce.rs). Bumps deferred_fork_count only; tallies NO solver forks on either branch.
(4) core_outcome_handlers::process_deferred_forks_into_core — parallel mirror of (3).
Functionally equivalent for correctness; do NOT unify without an explicit decision (would either lose profiling or add it everywhere).
solver_fork_count therefore has exactly THREE tally sites: (1), (2), and SimulationLoop::dispatch_bounce's BounceKind::Hook arm (the pre-callback state-snapshot fork before bouncing to a Python SimProcedure — NOT a deferred fork). The no-condition conservative state.fork() in (1)/(2) DOES clone a solver but is never tallied, so deferred_fork_count and solver_fork_count are siblings, not sub/superset (see also avoid-early-return-on-empty-deferred-forks). run_loop.rs no longer mentions deferred forks at all — pre-angr-nbim4.3 citations pointing there are stale. Doc comments on both counters live on the stats-macro fields in interpreter/mod.rs and were re-anchored to these symbol names in angr-9ke6b.86 (commit 5b2c58432).

invariant-symbolic-bitcount-sound-export: Symbolic clz/ctz/popcount export from Rust->claripy MUST be tied to the operand AST, not a fresh BVS. claripy_bridge/export/ast_helpers.rs::build_sound_bitcount (moved there by the angr-5mnx3.11 split; was claripy_bridge/export.rs post zel8z.5, and claripy_bridge.rs before that) emits a sound encoding for width<=64: nested If(Extract(i,i,operand)==1, count, ...) for clz (LSB->MSB so MSB test is outermost) and ctz (MSB->LSB so LSB test is outermost); popcount is sum of ZeroExt(w-1, Extract(i,i,operand)). Result width == operand width (matches the concrete BVV(result,width) fast path). width>64 keeps the fresh-BVS fallback (record_export_unconstrained_clz). Pre-fix a fresh unconstrained BVS per call meant Python-side eval could return Rust-infeasible values AND identity was unstable. See angr-acoq.

invariant-symbolic-byte-lane-lookup: SymbolicMemory sidecar invariant, BOTH directions. READ side: `symbolic_objects` is keyed ONLY at a symbolic object's BASE address; `symbolic_spans` is the reverse index mapping every covered byte back to (base, width). Any code that reads a byte the page bitmap marks symbolic MUST do load.rs::try_byte_merge_load's two-step lookup — `symbolic_objects[byte]` (take lane 0 via `SymbolicMemory::extract_byte_lane`), else `symbolic_spans[byte]` -> `symbolic_objects[base]` + `extract_byte_lane(offset)` — and must NEVER use the base-keyed map alone. Doing so is doubly wrong: interior bytes miss and fall through to the page's concrete placeholder (content silently discarded), AND the base byte yields the WHOLE wide object rather than its 8-bit lane, which then feeds mismatched widths into `RustBV::ite_into` (debug_assert only — a release build constructs a malformed-width Ite). This is the same 'bitmap says symbolic, sidecar lookup is base-only' family as angr-c7xno.50 and angr-91vj9.3; it recurred in `merge.rs::merge_byte_value` (angr-0jh0j.30), now fixed via the `symbolic_byte_lane` helper. Reuse `extract_byte_lane` (pub(super) in load.rs; takes no SymContext since angr-6cp06.63) rather than reimplementing a simplified version — the endness handling is not obvious. Every merge test predating the fix used width-8 symbolic values, which is why it went undetected; any new per-byte memory test should use a >1-byte symbolic object. WRITE/REMOVAL side (the mirror, angr-6cp06.63): code that supersedes ONE byte must not spell the cleanup as `symbolic_objects.remove(&addr)` + `symbolic_spans.remove(&addr)`. Exact-key removal misses a WIDER container based below `addr` (which keeps claiming the superseded byte, then races the fresh value on export, where `_get_state_symbolic_z3_asts` emits both with no containment ordering), and when `addr` IS a container base it orphans the interior spans. Call `SymbolicMemory::retire_symbolic_object_at` (symbolic_objects.rs), which resolves the covering object either way, drops it, and re-inserts every OTHER covered byte as an 8-bit lane inheriting `imported_addrs`. Splitting into lanes beats `store_concrete`'s older angr-7qon recovery, which could only reclassify the survivors as concrete.

invariant-symbolic-store-no-zero-bytes: Symbolic store/load forwarding in the VEX interpreter (native/angr/src/interpreter) has a soundness invariant fixed in angr-ofyh (commit 5c4974162): the buffered fast path must NOT push bv_to_bytes(bv) into the byte-indexed pending_stores for symbolic data — bv_to_bytes yields all-zeros for symbolic values, so an offset load inside the store would silently return concrete 0. EVERY insert site into pending_symbolic_stores must call evict_overlapping_symbolic_stores first: statements_store.rs (handle_concrete_store + buffer_store_for_rust_memory, angr-vvzf5) AND cas_store_symbolic_data in statements_cas.rs (concrete-addr/no-callback branch, angr-myzjx.27 — the last un-evicted clone site). UPDATE (angr-9ke6b.19, commit 69c0ef344): cas_store_symbolic_data's concrete-addr/no-callback branch is now reachable only for CONCRETE data_bv — a symbolic value there hard-errors via reject_symbolic_byte_store before the pending_symbolic_stores insert. invariant-syscall-byte-cap-shared: Native byte caps: every handler that bounds a concrete byte count before falling back to Python MUST source it from syscalls/mod.rs::MAX_IO_SIZE (4096), not a local literal. Convention is an alias-import so each call site keeps its own vocabulary: syscalls/read.rs 'MAX_IO_SIZE as MAX_READ_SIZE', syscalls/write.rs 'as MAX_WRITE_SIZE', cgc.rs 'as MAX_CGC_BYTES' (transmit/receive/random), startup.rs 'as MAX_GETRANDOM', and the stdio trio procedures/fread.rs 'as MAX_FREAD_SIZE', fwrite.rs 'as MAX_FWRITE_SIZE', fgets.rs 'as MAX_FGETS_SIZE' (angr-0jh0j.45); fd_io.rs uses the bare name and applies it PER SEGMENT for readv/writev. This spans BOTH implementations of the same request: the libc-hook twins procedures/read.rs and procedures/write.rs alias it too (angr-03vl4.49) -- they had kept independent 4096s, so a cap bump would have desynced the libc path from the syscall path. angr-myzjx.18 established this for syscalls read/write/fd_io; angr-9ke6b.157 swept in cgc/startup. Distinct families, do NOT merge: the str-family SCAN cap is procedures/strings.rs::MAX_STRING_SCAN (same alias convention, e.g. strchr.rs 'as MAX_SCAN', strlen.rs 'as MAX_STRLEN', puts.rs 'as MAX_PUTS_LEN'; stdio.rs::MAX_FPUTS_LEN stays a named const derived from it because its byte-offset loop needs u64), and the printf/scanf format-string cap is procedures/format_common.rs::MAX_FORMAT_LEN. DECIDING TEST for which home a 4096 belongs to -- does the C function take a length/size argument? If yes it is a request-size cap (MAX_IO_SIZE); if no, the cap only exists to bound a NUL scan (MAX_STRING_SCAN, or MAX_FORMAT_LEN when the scanned thing IS the format string). Note the split INSIDE the printf family: the format string uses MAX_FORMAT_LEN, but a %s conversion *argument* is a plain C string and uses MAX_STRING_SCAN (sprintf.rs::format_string, pinned by sprintf_tests::test_sprintf_percent_s_scan_bounded_by_max_string_scan). All three are 4096 today, so picking wrong is invisible until someone lowers one. New handlers: alias, don't redefine. ANTI-PATTERN, do not 'fix' this in a future audit round: never add a compile-time or unit-test assertion that any two of these caps are numerically EQUAL. Their independence is the whole point -- a security-driven reduction of one is expected to move only its own family (angr-0jh0j.87 was filed as an inconsistency for exactly this and resolved with documentation, not an equality pin).
invariant-syscall-fd-check-before-count: INVARIANT for native syscall handlers (native/angr/src/syscalls/): validate the fd/handle argument BEFORE any size- or count-based early return that reports SUCCESS. The Python reference procedures resolve the descriptor first (e.g. procedures/cgc/receive.py::run does posix.get_fd(fd) -> -1 before touching count), so any native handler that short-circuits on count==0/len==0 ahead of the fd check reports SUCCESS for a never-opened fd and silently mis-models it as valid — a wrong-answer divergence with no Python fallback and no diagnostic. Fixed in NativeReceiveSyscall::call (angr-fs583); NativeTransmitSyscall::call already had the right order. It is NOT a blanket fd-before-count rule: both CGC handlers deliberately check count > MAX_CGC_BYTES first, which is safe only because that arm returns the same Python-fallback Err an invalid fd would (angr-6cp06.56 narrowed cgc.rs's comment, which had generalized this to 'every count-based short-circuit'). So the test is the early return's RESULT, not its position: an Err/fallback may precede the fd check, an Ok must not. When adding or reviewing a handler with an early-out on a zero size, check the fd!=0/is_open() test precedes it, and pin it with a test that exercises the invalid-fd + zero-length COMBINATION — per-argument tests in isolation (fd==0,count==0 and fd!=0,count!=0) miss this entirely.

Test solver-distinctness (assert ret1!=ret2 is SAT via a fresh z3::Solver), NOT just distinct RustBV ids. angr-8o7w. The procedures side has TWO helpers over the same symbol_counter: use them rather than re-spelling the mint by hand. syscalls::support::fresh_symbolic for a plain mint, and procedures::fresh_zero_extended_symbol(state, prefix, src_bits, ext_bits) for the 'unconstrained value narrower than the C return type' shape (rand: 31->32, system: 8->32). Note ext_bits is the TOTAL target width for RustBV::zero_extend, while claripy's zero_extend takes the count of ADDED bits -- which is why the Python procs read zero_extend(sizeof(int) - 8) for the same thing (angr-6cp06.13).

invariant-widen-audit-gate-convert-not-e: When a baseline-gated audit script (tools/audit_*.py) is widened onto a directory that lights up with many pre-existing sites, prefer CONVERTING the sites to the gate's sanctioned safe spelling over annotating each with a per-line exemption marker. N per-line 'overflow-ok:'/'sp-default-ok:'/'page-shift-ok:' comments are worse than no gate: they are pure noise, they train reviewers to add one reflexively, and the gate then proves nothing. The ONE rationale goes in a module-level doc section (register_file.rs's '# Range arithmetic'), not repeated at each site. Two loops additionally lost their index arithmetic entirely by iterating a bounds-checked slice -- the safest conversion is often deleting the arithmetic, not respelling it. Corollary: keep these baselines empty. If a directory genuinely cannot be converted, the bead's third option (record why it stays out of SCAN_DIRS) beats a blanket file-scoped exemption marker, which would silently cover future new arithmetic too.

invariant-z3-ast-sort-check-before-wrap:
Raw Z3 AST extraction (extract_z3_ast_ptr, native/angr/src/solver/z3_ast_extract.rs) returns a Z3_ast with NO sort check. Consumers must verify sort before wrapping: BV::wrap over a Bool-sorted node (or Bool::wrap over a BV) is a wrong-sort Z3 call that trips Z3's error handler = PROCESS ABORT, not a recoverable PyErr. claripy Bools that claripy_to_rustbv cannot lower (e.g. fpEQ float comparisons) have length=None and reach these raw fast paths. Fix pattern: Z3AstPtr::sort_kind()/is_bool()/bv_width() (in symbolic/z3_ast_ptr.rs, via z3_sys::Z3_get_sort+Z3_get_sort_kind+Z3_get_bv_sort_size). NOTE (angr-9ke6b.202, 2026-08-02): the old is_bv() predicate was DELETED -- use bv_width(), which returns Some(width) exactly when the AST is BV-sorted, i.e. one call gives both the wrap precondition AND the authoritative width. Never read the width from claripy's .length instead: the sort is what BV::wrap is constrained by, and .length can be absent/disagreeing.

UPDATE (angr-9ke6b.203, commit 988144fc1): on the EVAL paths this whole dance is centralized in the free fn z3_ast_to_eval_bv(&Z3AstPtr) -> Option<RustBV>. Its 3 callers are eval_upto (parent solver.rs), eval_z3_ast_ptr and ast_to_bv_for_eval. TRAP when touching it: ast_to_bv_for_eval must keep DECLINING Bool (explicit early 'if z3_ast.is_bool() { return None }') rather than adopting the shared lowering -- its caller eval_batch falls back to Python, which yields a Python bool for a Bool-sorted AST, so returning 0/1 from Rust would silently change eval_batch's result type.
